# Dual Battery Isolator Setups

## Summary

[Partial] Decide between a marine-style isolator setup or parallel wiring with manual switches. [t2163]

[Partial] Install a solenoid and connect its trigger wire to stay hot only while the motor runs. [t2163]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Decide between a marine-style isolator setup or parallel wiring with manual switches.
2. [Partial] Determine if the goal is to keep batteries charged equally (isolator) or run one until drained (switch).
3. [Partial] Select battery types, noting that Odyssey 1200s fit side-by-side while Die Hard Platinum series may require relocation of parts like the power steering reservoir.

_Procedure reported by [t2163]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2163] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install a 200-amp solenoid to separate the two batteries when the truck is off.
2. [Partial] Connect the solenoid trigger wire to a feed that stays hot only while the motor runs, avoiding power during cranking.

</details>

## Parts

- 165-amp alternator, implied need [t2163]

- Die Hard Platinum Series 34 Battery: May require part relocation to fit [t2163]
- Dual Battery Isolator, e.g., IBS or Blue Sea [t2163]
- Odyssey 1200 Batteries: Preferred for under-hood fitment [t2163]

## Specifications

- **Alternator capacity (context)**: 165amp [t2163] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Isolator amp rating**: 200amp [t2163] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Consider the 'Usage side' vs. 'Charging side' distinction when selecting a management system. [t2163]
- [Partial] Use an isolator for automatic charging of both batteries; use manual switches if you prefer draining one battery completely before switching. [t2163]
- Use an override switch inside the cab to allow self-boosting without disconnecting batteries. [t2163]
- Connect winch ground directly to the battery post for shorter, more solid connections. [t2163]
